contract: Subclasses should override this method if the underlying cache system supports bulk retrieval operations (such as Memcached's getMulti or Redis's MGET).

constructors.signature: public ChronicleMap() throws RejectedExecutionException, IllegalStateException
constructors.javadoc_summary: Creates a ChronicleMap-compatible cache with default settings: capacity of 1024 entries, an eviction scan delay of 60,000 ms (1 minute), and the default TTL/idle times defined by `Cache#DEFAULT_LIVE_TIME` (3 hours) and `Cache#DEFAULT_MAX_IDLE_TIME` (30 minutes).

throws.condition: if the pool's maintenance scheduler rejects the eviction task
if the JVM is already shutting down when the underlying pool registers its shutdown hook

examples:
ChronicleMap<String, String> map = new ChronicleMap<>();   // capacity 1024, 60s eviction delay
map.stats().capacity();                                    // returns 1024 (default capacity)
map.isClosed();                                            // returns false (freshly created)
map.put("k", "v");                                         // returns true (stored with default 3h TTL / 30min idle)
String value = map.getOrNull("k");                         // returns "v"
map.getOrNull("absent");                                   // returns null (key not present)
map.getOrNull((String) null);                              // throws IllegalArgumentException (key must not be null)
map.close();                                               // stops this cache's background eviction task

examples:
ChronicleMap<String, Integer> map = new ChronicleMap<>(1_024, 60_000L);   // capacity 1024, 60s eviction delay
map.stats().capacity();                                                   // returns 1024 (capacity reflected in stats)

methods.javadoc_summary: Retrieves a value from the distributed cache by its key.
methods.returns: the cached value, or `null` if not found, expired, evicted, circuit breaker is open, or on error
contract: This method implements circuit breaker pattern to protect against cascading failures when the distributed cache becomes unavailable.
Callers that require availability diagnostics must monitor the breaker warning and backend health separately.

Open (Failing Fast): When at least one failure has been recorded, the recorded failure count is at least `maxFailuresBeforeCircuitOpen`, AND the time since the last failure is less than `retryDelay` milliseconds (so a `retryDelay` of `0` never fails fast), this method returns `null` immediately without attempting cache access.

A failure counts as interrupt-caused only while the calling thread's interrupt status is still set and its causes or suppressed exceptions (searched transitively: Jedis reports a failed connect attempt, and a Redis Cluster's random-node fallback reports each node's failed pool wait, only as suppressed exceptions) include an `InterruptedException`, `java.nio.channels.ClosedByInterruptException`, an `java.io.InterruptedIOException` other than `java.net.SocketTimeoutException` (a socket timeout is a backend failure), or the `java.net.SocketException` with the message `"Closed by interrupt"` that `java.net.Socket` throws when an interrupt closes a virtual thread's blocking socket (as it does for a bundled Jedis client's read or connect on a virtual thread); any other failure on an interrupted thread is still counted.
The bundled Jedis clients re-assert the interrupt status that Jedis clears when an interrupt ends its connection-pool wait, so such a failure qualifies as well.

An `Error` thrown by the client is not caught: it propagates and leaves the breaker state unchanged A read that was already in flight when `#close()` began and then fails (typically because close disconnects the client) is reported as a miss without touching the breaker state The closed-to-open transition is logged once at WARN level Thread Safety: This method is thread-safe.

methods.name: close
methods.signature: public synchronized void close()
methods.javadoc_summary: Permanently shuts down this cache wrapper and disconnects its owned client from all distributed cache servers.
contract: Cache wrappers and their pooled clients should normally be retained and shared; do not call this method after each request or cache operation.

Note that the bundled `SpyMemcached` client runs a non-daemon I/O thread, so an application that relies on the JVM exiting once its own threads finish (rather than on `System.exit` or a signal) must close the cache for the JVM to exit.

An operation already in flight when `close()` runs is not excluded: it may complete normally, or surface the underlying client's own exception (e.g., a "shutting down" error) instead of `IllegalStateException`.

⚠️ Best-effort disconnect: if the underlying client's disconnect throws an exception, this method logs it and still leaves this wrapper permanently closed; client-side connections or threads may therefore require external diagnosis.

methods.javadoc_summary: Creates a new builder for constructing `ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache` instances.
methods.returns: a new `Builder` instance initialized with default configuration values
examples:
// Basic configuration
ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache<String, Data> cache = ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache.<String, Data>builder()
    .capacityInMB(100)             // 100MB off-heap (= 100 * 1048576 bytes); required, must be positive
    .evictDelay(60000)             // scan for expired entries every 60s
    .defaultLiveTime(3600000)      // default 1h TTL
    .defaultMaxIdleTime(1800000)   // default 30min idle timeout
    .build();                      // allocates native memory now; returns a ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache

// Advanced configuration with disk spillover
// OffHeapStore is an interface; supply your own implementation (e.g., a file-backed store).
OffHeapStore<String> diskStore = myFileBackedOffHeapStore(Paths.get("/tmp/cache"));
ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache<String, byte[]> advancedCache = ForeignMemoryOffHeapCache.<String, byte[]>builder()
    .capacityInMB(200)             // 200MB off-heap
    .maxBlockSizeInBytes(16384)    // 16KB max block; larger values split across blocks
    .evictDelay(30000)             // scan every 30s
    .vacatingFactor(0.3f)          // evict 30% of entries (LRU first) under memory pressure
    .offHeapStore(diskStore)       // spill to disk when memory is full
    .statsTimeOnDisk(true)         // track disk read/write timing
    .build();                      // returns an application-scoped cache with disk spillover enabled

methods.javadoc_summary: Stores a key-value pair with the specified expiration settings.
methods.returns: `true` if the value was stored (in memory or on disk); `false` otherwise
contract: The value is serialized and placed in off-heap memory; when memory is unavailable (or the `storeSelector` directs it), the value is written to the configured `OffHeapStore` instead.

Values that could not be placed even in an otherwise empty cache — because the serialized form exceeds the entire off-heap capacity, or because its slot-rounded chunks need more 1 MB segments than the region has — never attempt the in-memory placement (no amount of vacating could make them fit) and go straight to the disk fallback, if any; such a doomed put schedules no vacate pass and leaves the in-memory cache contents untouched.
Key requirements: keys must implement `hashCode`, `equals`, and, for a `Comparable` key, `compareTo` consistently and without throwing.
The internal index also calls them while serving other keys' operations (`compareTo` when a bin of colliding keys is converted to a tree), so such a failure can surface from a put of another key.

If that removal fails (the key's lookup fails again, or the store's `remove` throws), the bytes, unreachable through the cache, are removed by a later `#clear()` or by `#close()` (if the store's `remove` fails during `close()`, that failure is logged and the bytes stay).

Until then the cache keeps a reference to each such key, and logs a warning when their number first reaches 1,024 and again each time it doubles; the count restarts once a `clear()` has removed them all.

The internal index also calls them while serving other keys' operations (`compareTo` when a bin of colliding keys is converted to a tree), so such a failure can surface from a put of another key.

// Basic cache with required fields

    .capacityInMB(200)
    .evictDelay(60000)
    .vacatingFactor(0.3f)

types.name: OffHeapCacheStats
types.javadoc_summary: An immutable snapshot of off-heap cache statistics at a specific point in time.

record_components.name: capacity
record_components.javadoc: a theoretical upper bound on the number of memory-resident entries, derived from the off-heap memory budget as `allocatedMemory / MIN_BLOCK_SIZE` (currently `allocatedMemory / 64`), capped at `Integer#MAX_VALUE`: every such entry occupies at least one 64-byte slot. Entries above 64 bytes need larger or additional slots, so off-heap memory typically fills long before the memory-resident count (`size - sizeOnDisk`) approaches this value. It does not bound `size`, which also counts disk-spilled entries.

record_components.name: size
record_components.javadoc: the current number of entries in the cache, counting both memory-resident and disk-spilled entries. To compute the memory-only entry count, use `size - sizeOnDisk`.

record_components.name: sizeOnDisk
record_components.javadoc: the current number of entries whose value bytes are stored on disk via the configured `OffHeapStore`. These entries are still counted in `size`; only their payloads live on disk.

record_components.name: putCount
record_components.javadoc: the total number of successful put operations since cache creation, counting values stored in off-heap memory and values written to the disk store. A put that throws after its value was already mapped is counted. A put that fails (e.g., neither memory nor disk could accept the value) is not counted; internal disk-to-memory promotions are not counted either.

record_components.name: putCountToDisk
record_components.javadoc: the number of put operations that resulted in writing data to disk. This occurs when off-heap memory is full, or the value can never fit in off-heap memory, and the value is stored to disk via the configured `OffHeapStore`, or when the `storeSelector` explicitly routes the value to disk. It is a subset of `putCount`.

record_components.name: getCount
record_components.javadoc: the total number of lookups classified as a hit or miss since cache creation. Failures before that classification (such as a throwing store read or a corrupt payload length) are not counted. Conceptually, `getCount = hitCount + missCount`; the sum saturates at `Long#MAX_VALUE` if the two counters would overflow.

record_components.name: hitCount
record_components.javadoc: the number of get operations that found a live entry and its bytes. A get that finds a disk-backed entry whose backing bytes are confirmed missing counts as a miss, not a hit. To approximate hits served purely from off-heap memory, subtract `hitCountFromDisk` from `hitCount`. A get that found live bytes but then threw during deserialization remains counted here because exceptional reconstruction is not tracked separately.

record_components.name: hitCountFromDisk
record_components.javadoc: the number of get operations whose value was successfully reconstructed from bytes read from the configured `OffHeapStore`. It normally forms a subset of `hitCount`, but independently sampled counters can be transiently inconsistent.

record_components.name: missCount
record_components.javadoc: the number of failed get operations where the entry was not found in either memory or disk. This can occur when the key never existed, was explicitly removed, has expired, or still had a cache mapping whose backing-store bytes were missing. A lookup that finds an entry just as a concurrent operation removes or replaces it also counts as a miss.

record_components.name: evictionCount
record_components.javadoc: the total number of entries removed because they expired (lazily on access or by the periodic maintenance sweep) or were reclaimed by the memory-pressure vacate pass. Explicit `remove()` / `clear()` calls and `put()` replacements are NOT counted here.

record_components.name: evictionCountFromDisk
record_components.javadoc: the number of disk-stored entries removed because they expired (lazily on access or by the maintenance sweep). The vacate pass evicts only memory-resident entries, so it never contributes here. Explicit `remove()` / `clear()` and `put()` replacements of a disk-stored key are NOT counted here.

record_components.name: allocatedMemory
record_components.javadoc: the total allocated off-heap memory in bytes. This is the fixed amount of native memory reserved for the cache at creation, organized into fixed-size segments.

record_components.name: occupiedMemory
record_components.javadoc: the currently occupied off-heap slot space in bytes. This includes serialized data plus slot-rounding/alignment padding, but not the heap-resident entry metadata.

record_components.name: dataSize
record_components.javadoc: the total size of actual serialized data tracked by the cache in bytes, across both the off-heap memory pool and the disk store, excluding any slot-allocation padding or internal overhead. To isolate the in-memory portion, subtract `dataSizeOnDisk` from `dataSize`.

record_components.name: dataSizeOnDisk
record_components.javadoc: the total size of serialized data currently stored on disk in bytes. This is a subset of `dataSize` and counts only entries that have been persisted to disk storage.

record_components.name: writeToDiskTimeStats
record_components.javadoc: statistics for successful disk-spilled put operations, tracking the minimum, maximum, and average time in milliseconds. The measured window is the store write (`OffHeapStore.put()`) itself, excluding serialization, the preceding failed in-memory slot search, and the entry installation - the write counterpart of `readFromDiskTimeStats`. Timing observations are recorded only when the cache is built with `statsTimeOnDisk(true)` (it defaults to `false`); when disabled, no observations are ever recorded and all three values stay `0.0`.

record_components.name: readFromDiskTimeStats
record_components.javadoc: statistics for disk read operations, tracking the minimum, maximum, and average time in milliseconds for reading entry bytes from the store. The measured window is the store read (`OffHeapStore.get()`) itself; lookups that never reach the store (entry already removed or replaced concurrently), throwing store reads, and corrupt-length results are not recorded. Confirmed store misses are recorded. Timing observations are recorded only when the cache is built with `statsTimeOnDisk(true)` (it defaults to `false`); when disabled, no observations are ever recorded and all three values stay `0.0`. This helps monitor disk read performance and cache hit efficiency.

record_components.name: segmentSize
record_components.javadoc: the size of each memory segment in bytes. The off-heap memory is organized into fixed-size segments (the built-in caches always use 1MB = 1048576 bytes) to manage memory allocation and reduce fragmentation.

record_components.name: occupiedSlots
record_components.javadoc: a detailed map showing memory slot occupation across segments. The outer map's key is the slot size in bytes - any multiple of the 64-byte minimum block size up to `maxBlockSize` (e.g., 64, 128, 192, 256, 320,...), not only powers of two - and the inner map contains segment index as key and the number of occupied slots in that segment as value. This provides granular visibility into memory fragmentation and utilization patterns.

methods.returns: `true` if an entry was deleted from Memcached for this target (regardless of which client originally acquired the lock), `false` if no entry existed (e.g., the lock had already expired or was never acquired)
contract: It's important to always unlock in a finally block to ensure locks are released even if exceptions occur.

If your TTL is short relative to how long the critical section may take (due to GC pauses, scheduling, network jitter), the original holder's lock can expire and be reacquired by a second client before the first client's unlock call runs — at which point the first client deletes the second client's lock and a third client may immediately acquire it.

Interruption: like `java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock#unlock()`, the release is attempted even if the calling thread's interrupt status is already set (for example, in the `finally` block of a cancelled task).
